text: A dilute single chain in three dimensions has N+1 classical point beads; bead 0 is pinned at the origin. There is no bending energy, excluded volume, other interparticle interaction or background flow.
Adjacent beads have identical isotropic central spring potentials k_s*(|r_j-r_(j-1)|-b)^2/2. The same unknown rest length b applies to all preparations.

At each finite spring stiffness the full Cartesian canonical equilibrium is established with an ordinary heat reservoir at T. Readouts then take k_s to infinity at fixed finite N,b,T and other controls. This fixes the configurational angular measure without invoking an exactly constrained kinetic Hamiltonian.
In force mode a known constant force F in +x acts on the last bead through potential -F*x_N; measure its equilibrium mean x-coordinate.

In clamp mode the last bead has potential K*(x_N-X)^2/2, with y_N and z_N free. Measure the signed mean +x force K*(X-x_N) exerted by the clamp on the chain. Equilibrate for finite k_s,K, first take k_s to infinity at fixed K, then take K to infinity at fixed X. No separate endpoint position or radial constraint is present.

readouts.clamp_mode: limiting equilibrium mean signed +x force from the uniaxial harmonic clamp

eventual_instruction: Use the established neutral instruction explicitly allowing replacement of all implementation helpers. No prescribed solver or derivative formula.
